cases.case: Announcements: none on load or over 65 s healthy
cases.rule: From the page load (the recorder attaches before the page's scripts run), through its first Live and 65 s of healthy polls and a state message: zero mutations of #announce. Markup: the only live region on the page is #announce (role status, aria-live polite, aria-atomic true), a child of body with no hidden ancestor; #linkstate, #log-count and every other element have no live-region attribute and no live-region ancestor. Automation verifies markup, mutations and announcement text and timing, not what a screen reader says

cases.case: Announcements: a disconnect, its retries and the recovery (SIGSTOP 24 s, then SIGCONT)
cases.rule: The simulator stopped about 24 s past the disconnect. Each transition says exactly its own announcement: the disconnect 'Disconnected. Reason: ...'; each retry as it starts and as it fails NOTHING (Task 54), while the banner changes in that render ('Reconnecting now.' as it starts, 'Retrying in N s' as it fails); so the whole time down says one announcement, the disconnect; never the same text twice in a row; the connection's return before its first state nothing; the recovery exactly once 'Connection restored; data current.'. Every #announce mutation is an announcement written with a transition (within 50 ms) or the clean-up of one 10 s later: none is a tick. Between transitions zero #announce mutations (but an announcement's clean-up), while in each interval of 2.5 s or more the banner's visible text changes about once a second (countdown, 'N s ago': at least the interval's whole seconds minus 2); no announcement holds a ticking value
